statement: The function returns a result r, and r (interpreted as a mathematical integer) is the maximum length of a good subsequence of nums. A good subsequence of nums is a non-empty sequence seq of integers of length m (with m >= 1) for which there exist indices 0 <= i_0 < ... < i_{m-1} < len(nums) such that seq[t] = nums[i_t] for every 0 <= t < m, and the number of t with 0 <= t < m-1 and seq[t] != seq[t+1] is at most k.
preconditions: nums is a slice of i64 with 1 <= len(nums) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; k is an i64 with 0 <= k <= min(50, len(nums)).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail.

statement: If maximum_length(nums, k1) returns r1 and maximum_length(nums, k2) returns r2, then r1 <= r2.

statement: If maximum_length(nums, k) returns r and maximum_length(nums2, k) returns r2, then r = r2.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are slices of i64 with 1 <= len(nums) = len(nums2) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 10^9; k is an i64 with 0 <= k <= min(50, len(nums)); for all i, j with 0 <= i < len(nums) and 0 <= j < len(nums), nums[i] = nums[j] iff nums2[i] = nums2[j].
